answer: To resist one-mind-many-masks sybils, tie each epoch's fresh challenge to a tight wall-clock deadline and demand several skilled answers at once. Picture a harbor where a single raven in many masks tries to crew every ship: one shared inference pipeline serializes, so its identities leak the same timing fingerprint across the whole ocean of seats, exposing them as copies of one agent. Faking N truly parallel identities then forces N independent inference stacks, erasing the cost saving that made running many masks from one mind worthwhile.
